answer.rationale: Write latency spike correlates directly with the 2-hour-old release under peak settlement load. Memory_b1 established that rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b6 confirms staged gating catches regressions quickly. Since we have only one intervention window and must preserve writes during peak settlement, rollback is the highest-confidence action: it's reversible, has proven success in this system, and eliminates the likely culprit (newly deployed code) while keeping the stable prior build operational. We verify memory_b1 to confirm rollback execution was clean and fast. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) would only mask the problem; capacity (memory_b3) takes too long; failover (memory_b2) risks introducing new latency vectors. Read replicas (memory_b5) don't address write-path degradation.
